claims.text: A combinatorial high-throughput mechanical-testing approach with systematic composition variation can identify alloying strategies for FeNiCrMn-based HEAs.
Some identified alloying strategies will increase yield strength by at least 10% without significantly compromising ductility.
The starting FeNiCrMn alloy will be in an as-cast or homogenized condition.
Minor additions such as Al or Cu will be varied incrementally at levels up to 10 at%.
Small, systematically fabricated libraries can produce composition gradients suitable for high-throughput screening.
Mechanical screening will be performed at room temperature under standard atmospheric conditions using microindentation, nanoindentation, and/or mini-tensile testing.
Alloying additions induce local microstructural changes, including precipitation and short-range ordering.
The alloying-induced microstructural changes affect dislocation dynamics and grain-boundary properties.
The relevant FeNiCrMn-based alloy has an underlying face-centered-cubic lattice.
Changing solute content modifies the face-centered-cubic lattice and controls precipitation behavior.
Solute-induced lattice and precipitation changes influence strain hardening and overall mechanical performance.
Certain examined compositional ranges will exhibit at least a 10% strength increase relative to undoped FeNiCrMn.
The strengthened compositions will maintain elongation and ductility above a threshold relative to the undoped baseline.
Undoped FeNiCrMn tested under identical conditions will serve as the performance control.
The proposed results are not necessarily applicable to long-term aging or extreme-temperature service.
Unanticipated phase formation or brittleness may reduce ductility or corrosion performance.
EBSD, XRD, or TEM can characterize grain structure and precipitate morphology and distribution in the composition-spread samples.
